The hexadecimal below is data encoded in the DEFLATE compression format (in raw form without any wrapper), and it can be used to calculate the total stopping time of the [Collatz function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collatz_conjecture) for a given input number.

```



```

To do so:

- Replicate the middle line of hexadecimal so that it appears a number of times equal to the desired input number.
- Repeatedly inflate the data, using the output of each inflation as the input for the next, until an error occurs due to the input data being invalid. (Note: this may take a large number of inflations!)
- Taking the most recent inflation output, count the number of occurrences of the below byte sequence; this number will be number of times the Collatz function must be applied in order to reach 1 starting from the input number that was entered.

```
a2b8e74ab10b28f602c561407120521c0b144723c5e980e28444714aa43829539c1728ce4c14e7468a0b558a4b248aeb468aeb46800002000000ffff000000ffff1aedb98ef65c0747cf152080000208208000020820800002082080000208208000020820800002082080000208208000020820800002000000ffff02000000ffff
```
